prerequisites: FUNDAMENTOS MATEMÁTICOS DE LA INGENIERÍA I
FUNDAMENTOS FÍSICOS DE LA INGENIERÍA I

learning_outcomes.text: Knows the basic principles of fluid mechanics and its application to solving problems in the field of engineering. Calculation of pipes, channels and fluid systems.

Distinguishes materials that behave as fluids and knows their characteristic properties. Understands the concept of pressure and identifies forces generated within a fluid and the force on surfaces. Deducts and applies the continuity equation, distinguishing volumetric and mass flow. Deducts and employs Bernoulli's equation. Calculates the Reynolds number and determines the type of flow. Formulates and solves the mechanical energy balance in fluid flow problems. Formulates and solves pipe system problems. Performs basic sizing and calculation of the fundamental parameters characterizing a fluid transport and distribution system.

syllabus_topics: Flow description: streamlines, pathlines, and streaklines. Velocity field properties
Integral methods in boundary layer theory
teaching_methods: Problem/exercise solving in the ordinary classroom
assessment_rules: The course is continuously assessed throughout the semester. Students who fail the continuous assessment can take a second call exam. To pass the second call, an individual exam must be passed with a score higher than 5 out of 10, covering the entire syllabus.
